relation: authenticated RDF (V5): SPARQL over Data Integrity credentials

evidence.command: cargo run --release --manifest-path zk/sparql-evaluator/Cargo.toml -p sparq-proved-evaluator --example paper_sweep --features authenticated-rdf -- --set sweep --suite eddsa --mode hidden --n 1 --size 32 --execute [--blank-free]
evidence.credential: one eddsa-rdfc-2022 credential of 32 statements, hidden signature mode

conditions: FILTER EXISTS and FILTER NOT EXISTS are admitted only when no credential in the presentation contains a blank node (model/src/v3/evaluate.rs).
Results are exact SPARQL 1.1 answers over the default graph formed by the presented credentials; there are no named graphs.

features.note: Credential data containing blank nodes is supported; blank-node labels are renamed per credential so credentials never share one.

features.query: PREFIX ex: <http://ex/> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT ?s WHERE { GRAPH ?g { ?s ex:name ?n } }
features.note: Admitted and evaluated as specified: the credentials form the default graph and the dataset has no named graphs, so GRAPH matches nothing.

features.query: PREFIX ex: <http://ex/> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT ?s FROM <http://ex/g> WHERE { ?s ex:name ?n }
features.note: Admitted and evaluated as specified: FROM names a graph the dataset does not hold, so the default graph is empty.

features.query: PREFIX ex: <http://ex/> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT ?s WHERE { SERVICE <http://ex/sparql> { ?s ex:name ?n } }
features.with_blank_node_data_rejection: GRAPH, SERVICE and LATERAL are not admitted

features.query: PREFIX ex: <http://ex/> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT ?n WHERE { [] ex:name ?n }
features.note: A blank node in a query pattern is an existential variable; this is an ordinary basic graph pattern.
